key_insight: Post-weld heat treatment substantially improves hardness and tensile strength of AA7075 friction stir welds, but abnormal grain growth still persists in the weld zone, especially the shoulder-driven region.
engineering_relevance: PWHT can be an effective route to recover mechanical performance in friction stir welded AA7075 joints, but process optimization must account for cooling condition, tool speed, and residual microstructural instability.
method: Friction stir welded AA7075 using multiple tool rotation speeds (600–1400 rpm).
Compared cooling conditions: air, water, quenching oil, and cutting fluid.
Applied post-weld heat treatment and measured microhardness, tensile properties, and fracture behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PWHT raised yield strength by more than 70% and ultimate tensile strength by about 35% for defect-free specimens, while also increasing and homogenizing microhardness.
watch_item: PWHT improved properties but did not eliminate abnormal grain growth, so weld-zone microstructure may remain vulnerable despite strength gains.
paper_title: Post-weld heat treatment of AA7075 friction stir welded joints manufactured under various tool rotation speeds and cooling conditions
